description:
Generate a chart from a natural language description and optional raw data, and return it as an inline base64-encoded image. Chart-Output's AI layer selects the chart type, builds the spec, and renders automatically.

Use this tool when: you have natural-language data or a plain description without pre-structured labels/datasets; you want Chart-Output to pick the best chart type automatically; you have raw tabular data (JSON array or CSV) and want a chart without manually extracting labels and datasets.
Do NOT use this tool when: you already have structured labels and datasets → use render_chart or render_chart_url instead; you need SVG or PDF output → those formats are not exposed by this tool; you need custom Chart.js options or extensions → use render_chart with extensions instead.
Behavior: this tool makes a remote API call to Chart-Output's AI endpoint and may consume render credits. Requires a Pro or Agency plan; it also has its own monthly allowance.

Returns: an inline base64 image. The response text reports the AI-selected chart type and generation time in milliseconds.
Errors: 401 — CHART_OUTPUT_API_KEY is missing or invalid. 403 — the plan does not include plain-English charts (the Free plan does not; Pro and Agency do); do NOT retry, tell the user and share the upgrade link. 402 — the monthly allowance for AI charts is used up; do NOT retry, tell the user. 400 — description is empty or data is malformed. 422 — the AI could not build a chart from this description; rephrase it or pass data. 429 — rate-limited; wait for Retry-After. Network error — chart-output.com is unreachable or timed out.
Limitations: only png, jpeg or webp. Custom Chart.js options, extensions, headers, and KPI strips are not available — use render_chart or render_card for those. Requires a Pro or Agency plan.
Example: render_chart_ai({ description: "Monthly revenue for 2024 as a green bar chart, growing from 12k in Jan to 28k in Dec", width: 800, height: 400 })

brand.description: Slug of a saved brand kit (call list_brand_kits to see them), for example "acme-dark". Applies the kit's palette, fonts and logo. Colors you send yourself (dataset colors, theme) win over the kit. An unknown slug is a 404 that lists the real ones. Preset kits (obsidian, linen, polar, studio, ember, harbor) go in extensions.brandKitId instead.

data.description: Optional raw data for the AI to use when building the chart. Accepts either a JSON array of objects (e.g. [{"month":"Jan","revenue":12000},{"month":"Feb","revenue":15000}]) or a CSV string (e.g. "month,revenue\nJan,12000\nFeb,15000"). If omitted, the AI generates plausible data from the description alone. Providing real data yields more accurate charts.

description.description: Natural-language description of the desired chart. Be specific about chart type, colors, and key trends for best results. Optionally specify axis labels and units. Examples: "Monthly revenue for 2024 growing from 12k to 28k, use a green bar chart" or "Pie chart of market share: Android 72%, iOS 27%, Other 1%". Max 2000 characters.

format.description: Output image format. "png" (default) — lossless, best for general use. "jpeg" — smaller file size, lossy. "webp" — modern format with good compression. SVG and PDF are not exposed by this tool; use render_chart or render_chart_url for those.

height.description: Output image height in pixels. Range: 100–4000. Default: 400. The longest edge × scale must fit your plan: 1200 px on Free, 3000 px on Pro and Agency (the API answers 403 above that). Use 400 for landscape, 500–600 for square or portrait layouts.

width.description: Output image width in pixels. Range: 100–4000. Default: 800. The longest edge × scale must fit your plan: 1200 px on Free, 3000 px on Pro and Agency (the API answers 403 above that). Use 1200 for widescreen dashboards, 400 for compact embeds.

name: render_chart_ai
